T1550.002.name: Pass-the-Hash
T1550.002.description: Adversary captures NTLM hash and uses it to authenticate without knowing the plaintext password. Indicators: EventCode=4624, LogonType=3 or 9, LogonProcessName=NtLmSsp or seclogo, SubjectUserSid=S-1-0-0.
T1550.002.response: Isolate source machine, reset compromised account password, check for lateral movement to other hosts.

T1070.001.name: Event Log Cleared
T1070.001.description: Adversary clears Windows Security event log to remove evidence of intrusion. Indicator: EventCode=1102. This is a critical signal — legitimate users rarely clear security logs.
T1070.001.response: Immediately investigate what happened before the log was cleared. Check other log sources (Sysmon, firewall). Treat as active incident.

T1053.005.name: Suspicious Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Adversary creates scheduled task in suspicious directory (Temp, AppData, Downloads) to maintain persistence. Indicator: EventCode=4698 with TaskContent pointing to unusual paths.
T1053.005.response: Identify and delete the scheduled task. Investigate what the task executes. Check for other persistence mechanisms.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Adversary uses legitimate credentials to gain access. Subtypes: external RDP/SMB login from non-private IP, suspicious failed logon reasons (bad password after lockout), logon from unusual source.
T1078.response: Verify with account owner if login was legitimate. If not, disable account and investigate scope of access.

T1069.name: Permission Groups Discovery
T1069.description: Adversary enumerates domain groups and permissions via LDAP queries to identify high-value targets. Indicator: EventCode=30 with LDAP SearchFilter for admin groups.
T1069.response: Identify the source of LDAP queries. If from unexpected host/user, investigate for active intrusion.

T1082.name: System Information Discovery
T1082.description: Adversary enumerates system and network information. Indicator: EventCode=4661 with SAM_USER/SAM_GROUP object access.
T1082.response: Correlate with other discovery events. Single occurrence may be benign, multiple events suggest active reconnaissance.

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
T1059.description: Adversary uses obfuscated scripts via mshta.exe, rundll32.exe, or stdin to execute malicious code. Indicator: EventCode=7045 with suspicious ImagePath patterns.
T1059.response: Terminate the malicious service. Investigate what the script executed. Check for additional payloads dropped.

brute_force.name: Brute Force
brute_force.description: Adversary attempts multiple failed logins to guess credentials. High failure count followed by success indicates compromise.
brute_force.response: Lock the targeted account, investigate source IP, check if credentials were used elsewhere.
